title: Tablet Punch Coatings & Microfinish | PharmaGlobalEng
description: Evaluate anti-stick tablet punch coatings and Microfinish against the formulation, existing tooling and cleaning process. Discuss suitability before replacement.
headline: Tablet Punch Coatings: Match the Treatment to the Release Problem
lead: A coating recommendation should explain what problem it is intended to address. PharmaGlobalEng offers coating evaluation and Microfinish Coating alongside polishing and restoration, with suitability assessed against the tooling and application.
service: Tablet Punch Coating Evaluation and Microfinish Coating
body:
Start with the problem, not the coating name

Is product building up across the face, collecting inside an engraving or accompanied by visible surface damage? Record the location and timing before selecting a candidate treatment. Include the existing coating specification and the history of the affected tools.

Anti-stick coatings are not interchangeable across all formulations. The substrate, formulation, environment and process are part of the selection.[1] A description such as “hard coating” or “low friction” is not a complete application specification.

Write a useful objective: fewer interruptions from a documented deposit, preservation of a defined surface condition, or an improvement against an agreed inspection criterion. Avoid beginning with a promise that one treatment will eliminate every form of sticking, picking or tablet breakage.

What a coating comparison should answer

Our evaluation discussion can include CrN, DLC, TiN, TiCN and the appropriate surface-engineering route. Confirm the exact system and its suitability for the proposed job rather than assuming that every option is appropriate for every tool.

A practical specification checklist for a coating inquiry
QuestionInformation to provideWhat the proposal should clarify
What is happening at the surface?Tablet and punch photographs, location, recurrence and prior trials.The specific issue the candidate treatment is intended to address.
What tooling is being treated?Material, drawing, dimensions, coating identity and service history.Suitability, preparation requirements and any limitations.
Which areas need treatment?The relevant face, engraving or other identified working area.Treated areas and how critical features will be protected and checked.
How is the tooling used and cleaned?Approved cleaning information, handling method and operating context.Compatibility questions that must be resolved before use.
What would count as improvement?Baseline observations and required product/tooling acceptance checks.The comparison method and the scope of any performance conclusion.

Ask for gaps to be identified explicitly. A quotation based only on tool quantity is not the same as an application review. Agree which documents and inspection results are needed before the treatment is selected.

Chrome plating and chromium nitride are different specifications

Do not use “chrome” as a catch-all description. Hard chromium and chromium nitride are listed as distinct tooling treatments by a tooling manufacturer.[2] Ask for the exact coating identity from the tool record or supplier specification.

In research on model ibuprofen formulations, chrome plating affected sticking differently at different compaction forces.[3] That study is not a performance guarantee for your product or evidence that a particular coating should always be preferred.

This page is not an offer of an unconfirmed chrome-plating service. For a requirement that specifically calls for chrome-plated tooling, send the existing specification so availability and the correct scope can be confirmed. A different coating should not be substituted just because its name sounds similar.

PharmaGlobalEng Microfinish Coating

Microfinish Coating is part of PharmaGlobalEng’s surface-engineering offering, alongside polishing and restoration work. Tell us about the existing surface, the tablet defect and the conditions in which the problem occurs so we can discuss whether that route is suitable.

For a Microfinish inquiry, the questions remain practical: what substrate is involved, which surfaces are to be treated, what condition is acceptable before work, and how will the finished tooling be assessed? Agree the job specification and the evidence needed for your application.

The service name should not replace the technical review. We need to understand the tooling condition and operating context before confirming treatment scope or turnaround. Existing tools that cannot meet the necessary requirements may need a different route.

Can existing coated punches be treated again?

Begin with the available records. Identify the original coating, prior stripping or recoating, polishing history and the condition of critical features. When the coating identity is unknown, treat that as an unresolved question rather than assigning a process from appearance alone.

Inspect the underlying tool as well as the surface layer. A proposal should explain whether additional examination, preparation or measurement is needed and what findings would prevent the work. Coating is not a way to conceal structural damage or make an unacceptable dimension disappear.

Before choosing between reconditioning and replacement, compare the inspection requirements, the intended result and the verification work. Saving the existing tooling is valuable only when it can remain suitable for its use. Do not let the replacement lead time override that decision.

Before ordering a replacement set: ask PharmaGlobalEng to assess whether the available tooling information supports a polishing, restoration or coating-evaluation route. A preliminary review is a starting point; the final recommendation may require physical inspection.

Surface finish alone does not establish release performance

A 2024 experimental study found different sticking behavior among tested punch surfaces even though their measured roughness was similar. It examined surface chemistry as well as roughness.[4] A bright finish or a single roughness value is therefore not a complete selection argument.

Ask how the proposed surface will be characterized for the job. Retain the inspection method, the locations assessed and the acceptance basis. Compare equivalent measurements before and after treatment rather than using photographs taken under different lighting as the only evidence.

Keep the cleaning and handling instructions with the tooling record. A trial is harder to interpret when the preparation differs between the reference and treated tools or when the cleaning history has not been recorded.

Plan the production comparison before treating the set

Define the defect or maintenance issue being evaluated. Record the baseline, sampling method, relevant operating conditions and observation period. Decide which product-quality and tooling checks the responsible teams require.

For a sticking-related comparison, useful records can include the location and timing of deposits, cleaning interruptions and the condition of the corresponding tablet face. For a surface-condition comparison, use the agreed inspection method and record the same regions of the tools.

Use a representative, approved trial rather than declaring a universal result from a short demonstration. If batch, speed or formulation conditions changed at the same time, state the limits of the comparison. The conclusion should say what was observed under the tested conditions.

Agree the documentation expected from the service and from your own production trial before work begins. This avoids a gap between a completed coating job and the evidence needed to approve its use.

Questions to settle before a coating order

Can you select a coating from a tablet photograph alone?

A photograph can help describe the problem, but the tooling specification, existing surface and process information may still be needed. Physical inspection can also be necessary before a treatment is recommended.

Does the hardest coating provide the best anti-stick result?

Hardness alone is not an application review. Ask how the candidate treatment addresses the specific problem and how its performance will be assessed under the relevant conditions.

Can a coating remove the need for replacement in every case?

No. A tool has to remain suitable for service. Integrity, dimensions, geometry, the existing condition and the proposed work all need to be considered before deciding whether it can be retained.

Request an application-specific coating discussion

Send the press and tooling details, coating records, defect photographs and a short account of the run. Include previous treatments and their results. Contact PharmaGlobalEng before shipping so scope, handling and expected turnaround can be agreed.
